query:
Photographic role: Place the notebook flat on the workbench immediately to the repairer's right, with its spine parallel to the bench edge.
Scene context: An adult repairer and one notebook.

diagnosis.reason: The unchanged query ranks craft locations and activity above spatial placement. Some useful existing relations are deep in the global pool, so exposure contributes. However the inspected full source pool has thin explicit conjunctions of object support plane, named actor intrinsic side, and object-to-surface orientation; notebook identity and workbench setting cannot supply those missing relationships. No claim of exhaustive absence is made from the discovery scan.

existing_candidates.limitation: Between two people does not establish support plane, lateral actor side, orientation or a one-person scene.

sources.title: Coventry et al. (2018), Cued by What We See and Hear: Spatial Reference Frame Use in Language
sources.supports: Original research distinguishes landmark-intrinsic axes from viewer-relative axes and demonstrates that viewpoint and object rotations have different consequences for spatial descriptions. This supports declaring the reference owner and axis; it does not prescribe the scenes below.

sources.title: Adobe, Still life photography for beginners
sources.supports: Photography education treats layouts of inanimate objects and camera angle as adjustable compositional choices. This supports separating scene arrangement from its image projection, without prescribing particular placements.

evidence.inventory_method: Scanned every positive global document without a slot/tag filter using notebook, support/contact, axis and placement relation patterns. Inspected eight complete CIDs through checked installed BodyReader plus photo_canonical_source.native(record). Separately inspected all 19 working prop_placement bindings for scope. The eight working content/conditions/effects equal their decoded installed counterparts. The text scan supplies leads, not proof of exhaustive absence.

confusion_boundaries: Actor-right and picture-right are different reference frames; a viewpoint change can alter picture side without moving the prop beside its actor.
A support relation needs the actual receiving plane and object contact; a workbench setting does not specify where its props rest.
Parallel to a named surface boundary is not necessarily horizontal in the final image. In-plane diagonal prop rotation is not a Dutch-angle camera change.

Flat broad-face support and an upright or leaning axis are placement/orientation; folded, open, damaged, wet or otherwise altered prop states need separate authorization. Candidate preconditions retain folded/map/umbrella and seated-person states.
The position/orientation effects attach to the prop, not to the worker’s skeleton, expression, profession, handedness or action. No right-side placement implies a right-handed person.
Object physical depth, image overlap, ownership and user reach are different claims. No scene here proves ownership, comfort, safety or functional success.
recommendations: Strengthen complete owner/surface/axis conjunctions across daily-use contexts rather than adding workshop synonyms.

Retain native source prerequisites for all referenced props/supports and actor posture. Proposed source guards use protocol roles and exact kinds; native review must resolve actual owners and verify property names/values before qualification. Their syntactic validity is not semantic approval.

Keep retrieval, source eligibility and final visible geometry separate. Root should rerun this exact unchanged query plus additional intents against the integrated source. Do not transfer a deep iconographic staff/elbow relation into a generic prop solely to improve recall.
